depiction.primary_object: upward path splitting into two diagonal arrows

readings.meaning: split, fork, or branch (path, code, or flow)
fork in the road or navigation turn
diverge, separate, or divide into two
decision point or choosing between two options

ambiguity: Closely resembles an unbroken fork-right/left navigation arrow or a git branch icon, and at small sizes the small break on the right branch is easy to miss.

modifier_semantics.meaning: detachment, branching off from the main leftward path

task_intents: fork a code repository or branch
split an item into two parts
plan a detour or alternate route
divide a shared bill or account

example_tasks.task: Split the 50lb bag of bread flour with Maria next door
Set up A/B routing rules for the new checkout page
Divide the utility bills between upstairs and basement tenants
Map out the high-water alternate trail around Twin Creek
Separate personal receipts from LLC expenses in the Q3 sheet
Decide whether to renew the lease for another year or move closer to downtown
Break the monolithic onboarding guide into separate tracks for engineers and designers
Figure out where the highway splits near Toledo so we don't miss the turnpike exit

example_tasks_es: Bifurcar el repositorio del cliente para probar el nuevo parche
Dividir los gastos del viaje a Bariloche entre los dos grupos
Elegir entre la ruta por la costa o la autopista de peaje

Write pros and cons list for public vs charter school

Drop off the rent check at the local bank branch
Saw down the dead oak branch overhanging the garage
Shuffle the summer road trip playlist

reasoning: A Y-shaped diverging arrow showing one path splitting into two (with the right branch slightly detached). It works well for tasks about branching code, splitting accounts or workflows, route forks/detours, and binary decisions, though it can be confused with unbroken split arrows or git merge/branch icons.
